edits.old: Atlas recommends assigning the minimum required permissions and using fine-grained custom database roles when predefined privileges are too broad; those roles can scope actions to particular databases and collections. (high confidence)
edits.new: Atlas recommends using fine-grained custom database roles for connecting to Atlas clusters, to provide granular scoping based on the access required and to follow the principle of least privilege. Custom roles can be created when the built-in roles don't include the desired set of privileges, and their privileges can be scoped to particular databases and collections. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/auth/authorization.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-add-mongodb-roles.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-customDbRoles-create.md

evidence.quote: For connecting to Atlas clusters, use fine-grained custom database roles to provide granular scoping based on the access required for the role to perform its function. This approach enables you to follow the principle of least privilege.

You can create custom roles in Atlas when the [built-in roles](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/built-in-roles.md#std-label-atlas-user-privileges) don't include your desired set of privileges.
List of actions per database and collection. If no database or collections are provided, cluster scope is assumed.

edits.rationale: The architecture guidance recommends fine-grained custom database roles for granular scoping and least privilege. The custom roles page says custom roles are for when built-in roles lack the desired privileges, and the CLI reference shows privileges are listed per database and collection. The original wording that these roles apply when predefined privileges are 'too broad' is a paraphrase: the source says built-in roles 'don't include your desired set of privileges'. The exact phrase 'minimum required permissions' also does not appear in the cited page.
